title: Prove exactly what a target build contains before release

requirements.invariant: A release candidate records one validated target environment/profile/channel, immutable repository/build identity, exact contract versions and a complete artifact/lock evidence set before it may be compared with staging evidence; constructing that record performs no distribution or production write.

Canonical manifest evidence includes schema/query/operation/Sync/catalog versions, dependency-lock hashes and immutable artifact hashes; local/staging/production order and feature authority remain separate gates rather than fields a build can self-authorize.

Release evidence contains only reviewed Ledger and standard Swift values; provider handles, signing material, mutable URLs/paths, dynamic dictionaries and backend SDK values cannot enter the manifest boundary.

Artifact creation, schema/contract compatibility and feature activation remain separate: a manifest can prove exact immutable inputs and compatibility without granting deployment, authority activation, cutover or destructive cleanup.

The manifest explicitly remains evidence-only and cannot represent cutover authorization; even an internally consistent production-profile manifest does not satisfy product, spike, security, physical-device, migration, backup, operator or source-freeze gates.

items: ReleaseApplicationVersion, ReleaseSourceRevision, ReleaseArtifactID and ReleaseSHA256 are validated bounded values; channel, platform, artifact kind and dependency ecosystem are closed enums.

ReleaseBuildIdentity derives environment/profile and exact schema/query/operation/Sync versions from ValidatedLedgerEnvironment and binds app version, build number, source revision and generated contract-catalog hash.

ReleaseArtifactEvidence contains stable artifact ID/kind/platform, positive byte count and SHA-256 only; pure byte verification detects changed size or content without opening a file, URL or provider object.
ReleaseDependencyLockEvidence contains one closed ecosystem plus bounded public lock identity and SHA-256; raw lock contents, paths and credentials are excluded.

LedgerReleaseManifest is created only through ReleaseManifestValidator from a draft, exact required artifact/lock sets and compatibility policy; it stores deterministically sorted evidence, a canonical content digest and an evidenceOnly authority disposition.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This provider-free evidence contract creates no Postgres relation, deployment table, view, function, constraint or index.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No release, deployment, upload, signing, activation or business command handler executes.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, view or function is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row or privileged function exists; future manifest retention/approval storage requires a separate security and operator-authority slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: Sync contract version is evidence only; no PowerSync Stream, deployment or client schema activation is defined.

items: A validated manifest encodes to deterministic sorted canonical bytes and reconstructs through the same validator without network, keychain, signer, provider SDK or mutable build-host state.

Reordered equivalent artifact/lock inputs normalize to the same manifest digest; changed bytes, hashes, required sets, environment/channel/profile, catalog/contract versions and duplicate identities fail atomically.
Canonical bytes contain no filesystem path, URL, credential, provider metadata, Principal, Account or product payload and stay below a fixed manifest-size ceiling.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Artifact byte hashing is pure evidence verification; this slice does not read/write Storage, local files, app media or release-provider objects.

appMcp.notApplicable: The shared target value contract is not wired to app, MCP or existing build/release tools; each later release adapter must consume the same validated manifest.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: A migration artifact may be listed by hash, but no Firebase export, transform, migration plan, reconciliation or production apply is created or authorized.

items: Stable failure codes distinguish invalid build identity, environment/channel confusion, contract/catalog mismatch, missing/duplicate artifact or lock evidence, byte/hash tamper and canonical-size overflow.

The manifest's evidenceOnly disposition and compatibility result are operational inputs only; no dashboard, alert, signer, operator sign-off, release provider or runbook activation exists in this slice.
Local, staging and production channels are bound to their matching validated environment/profile, while every accepted manifest remains evidenceOnly and cannot activate feature/backend authority.

The contracts are additive target-only Swift code/tests, import no provider SDK, alter no current app/release script, contact no hosted service, and can be reverted before release without changing an artifact or external state.

verification.expected: Closed release values, environment-derived build identity, exact catalog/contracts, required artifact/lock coverage, sorted canonical evidence, stable digest and evidence-only authority validate deterministically.
Equivalent reordered drafts create identical canonical bytes/digests, decode and revalidate offline, and pure artifact-byte verification preserves exact kind/platform/size/hash identity.

Wrong environment/profile/channel, contract/catalog mismatch, unsafe values, duplicates, missing/unexpected evidence, changed bytes/hash/size and oversized/noncanonical manifests fail with stable codes and no accepted partial manifest.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, all target tests, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent technical-control foundation derived from the platform capability dossier. It stops before signing/notarization keys, App Store/TestFlight/Sparkle/DMG adapters, SBOM generation, file I/O, provider credentials/resources, deployment, feature activation, migration/reconciliation execution, production release, cutover or operator approval.
